passages.note: House sponsor of the Religious Freedom Restoration Act as filed.
passages.actor_quote: Sponsored by: Rep. Timothy Wesco, Rep. Jud McMillin

passages.note: Yea on 3rd reading of the single-subject Religious Freedom Restoration bill.

passages.provision_quote: (b) A governmental entity may substantially burden a person's exercise of religion only if the governmental entity demonstrates that application of the burden to the person: (1) is in furtherance of a compelling governmental interest; and (2) is the least restrictive means of furthering that compelling governmental interest.
passages.note: Sec. 11 separately disclaims only a private cause of action against employers under this chapter; it does not establish a broader anti-discrimination carve-out covering employment and housing.

rows.reasoning: As House sponsor of SB 101 (2015) and with a Yea vote on its single-subject 3rd reading, Wesco acted for Indiana's Religious Freedom Restoration Act, whose operative standard bars government from substantially burdening a person's exercise of religion unless it proves a compelling interest and the least restrictive means. That strict-scrutiny exemption standard matches 'protect religious freedom and allow faith-based exemptions from laws that conflict with sincere religious beliefs,' not the unconditional organizational autonomy of rung 5 or the employment-and-housing anti-discrimination carve-out of rung 2.
